hero.title: Technology that serves people, not the other way around.
hero.paragraph1: Nordic Media Lab is the alliance helping entrepreneurs build ethical technology, and giving them the knowledge, funding, and shared infrastructure to stay independent.
hero.paragraph2: How we communicate, trust, and organise has slipped into the hands of a few companies whose incentives drifted far from ours. The Nordics know another way. We built cooperatives, folk high schools, and movements that put people before growth and kept the economy ethical. We made small countries strong by trusting one another. We are carrying that tradition into the digital world, and inviting everyone to join.

projects.title: Common Ground: Federating Nordic Media Lab
projects.intro1: Common Ground is a series of workshops exploring how Nordic Media Lab's members can be federated into a single network that lets us share in the network effects, without anyone losing their independence.
projects.intro2: The biggest barrier to launching new social platforms is the network effect. When you join a new platform you have few connections, and you eventually switch back to LinkedIn, Facebook, or one of the other giants, where everyone already is. The solution is not to build another competing giant, we would only face the same problems. It's to let many small platforms work as one network while each stays sovereign, the way email lets every provider talk without anyone owning the whole. The federated web is already being rolled out in various forms, and we want to take it to the next level.
projects.w1desc: Where we agree what that shared infrastructure must do, and the principles it must never break, before we choose a protocol that will unite us.
projects.w2note: We go deeper into the concrete protocols. More soon.

members.title: Become a member
members.description: We have three kinds of members in Nordic Media Lab: entrepreneurs building tech platforms, organisations that push for ethical and open-source technology, and individuals interested in changing our current technology landscape. You can join Nordic Media Lab for free. All we ask is that you support and work within our Nordic Media Pact. Here are our platforms and organisations:

cards.headline: Duckling
cards.text: Democratic media where young people can become journalists and storytellers. Alternative to Instagram and TikTok.

cards.headline: Oase
cards.text: A chat app without ads and endless feeds, designed to be a healthy alternative to Messenger and Snapchat.

cards.headline: Meningspunktet
cards.text: A new Danish social media focusing on credible conversations, digital well-being and data sovereignty, designed with people at the center. Alternative to Facebook.

cards.headline: Zen Social
cards.text: Online communities built for people, not consumers. Create a circle for your community in a simple, calm environment.

pact.title: To be a member, you must work for and support our common pact:
pact.mainDescription: With this pact, we declare that we work to develop and support technology that puts people before machines, community and privacy before profit, and transparency before manipulation. We thereby become part of Nordic Media Lab. We commit to:

transparency.title: Transparent business models
transparency.description: We work to ensure that our business models are open, understandable and fair. Users must know the terms - and have real power over their own data. Our solutions must give people control, not just consent boxes.

design.title: Design with conscience
design.description: We do not build technology for technology's sake. We design with people at the center - with respect for their attention, well-being and dignity. Users must be able to see through how the design affects them and have the opportunity to change it. We build on protocols, standards and technology where data can be freely exchanged and moved between platforms and services.

ownership.title: Organization and ownership
ownership.description: We will work for an organization and ownership that supports transparent business models and conscientious design. This means that we will do everything to ensure that our project or company cannot be sold to owners who work against the Nordic Media Pact. This can be, for example, through foundation ownership or by establishing a limited liability company, but can take many other forms.

beliefs.title: We believe:
items: That democratic infrastructure is a prerequisite for a free and enlightened society.
That collective ownership and cooperation create stronger and fairer solutions.
That long-term thinking and responsibility must prevail over short-term growth.

values.title: We are based on three Nordic values:

enlightenment.title: Enlightenment
enlightenment.description: We believe that technology and digital infrastructure must be based on insight, education and critical thinking. We work for an enlightened public, where we as citizens understand and can influence the systems that shape our everyday lives - including digital ones.

trust.title: Trust
trust.description: We believe that technology should be a tool for community, well-being and sustainable development. We make demands on how technology is designed, who benefits from it - and who is excluded. We support associations and other communities. We build digital communities that support physical communities.

cohesion.title: Cohesion
cohesion.description: We build digital infrastructure that thinks holistically and benefits both human systems and nature's ecosystems. We believe that openness, transparency and co-creation create better systems.

inspiration.folkHighSchool: <0>The Folk High School movement</0> created space for lifelong learning, reflection and personal enlightenment - not just for the elite, but for everyone. The movement also became part of the foundation for the Nordic welfare model.
inspiration.cooperative: <0>The Cooperative movement</0> showed that you can build strong economies and structures through community and shared responsibility - and still have room for capitalist business models.

team.title: How it started
team.story1: It started at the launch of Meningspunktet. Listening to Tue and Jacob lay out their vision for a healthier social platform, an idea that had been forming for months came into focus: the people building ethical alternatives shouldn't be doing it alone.
team.story2: That evening put several of them in the same room. Bjarke, who had met Jeppe of Zen Social a few months earlier, now also met Anders of Oase and Trine, an independent changemaker. The Nordics, and Denmark especially, have a long habit of punching above their weight, because we trust one another and know how to collaborate and compete at the same time. If a new era of ethical technology could begin anywhere, it could begin here.
team.story3: So Bjarke raised a hand and said it out loud: we should join forces. He went home and wrote up a first concept for Nordic Media Lab. Trine and Tue organised a follow-up dinner, the first of many gatherings among the five founders, Trine, Anders, Tue, Jeppe, and Bjarke. As word spread, more people joined, and it became clear the idea needed a home of its own. Tech lawyer Martin von Haller helped with the legal work, and Nordic Media Lab became real.
team.story4: That first meeting was about two years ago. We're still growing, fast.

privacy.title: How we handle your data
privacy.lede: A plain account of what we hold about you, why, and what you can do about it. No jargon, no small print, just the terms stated honestly.
privacy.who: Nordic Media Lab (forening), Denmark, is responsible for the data described here. If you have any question about your data, or want to see, correct, or remove it, write to us at <email>hej@nordicmedialab.dk</email>.
privacy.collect1: If you or your platform is a member, we hold your organisation's name, a short description, its website and logo, and the name, email, and role of the people who represent it. If you join as an individual, we hold your name, email, a short bio, and a link if you gave one. Where we are hoping to invite an organisation to join, we may hold a name, an organisation, an email, and a note of how we came across you. We also keep working notes as we run the network.
privacy.collect2: We do not collect anything we do not need. We keep no special-category data (nothing about health, beliefs, or the like).
privacy.why1: For two reasons, and only two. First, to communicate with members and run the network: to reach you, keep you informed, and organise our shared work. Second, to show approved member platforms on our website, so the movement is visible. Only the organisation itself appears publicly, its name, description, website, and logo. The personal contact details of the people behind it stay internal, and individual members are never listed publicly.
privacy.why2: We do not use your data for advertising or marketing, and we do not sell it or pass it to anyone for their own purposes.
privacy.basis: We rely on our legitimate interest in running the association and staying in contact with members and the people we hope will join, and, for members, on the membership relationship itself. Where we list your organisation publicly, we do so because you asked to be a member and a listing is part of that.
privacy.whereTitle: Who can see it, and where it lives
privacy.where: Only the Nordic Media Lab board and the people running the network can see the internal member database, which we keep in Airtable. Our website's code and its published content, which includes the public member listings and our board's own contact details, live in GitHub and are served to visitors by Netlify. These are all services that process data on our behalf under data-processing agreements. Airtable, GitHub, and Netlify are based in the United States, and those transfers are covered by the standard legal safeguards each provider offers.
privacy.keep: While you are a member or in contact with us. We remove your data when you ask us to, or when we no longer need it.
privacy.rights: You can ask to see the data we hold about you, correct it, object to how we use it, or have it deleted. Members can also correct their own listing at any time through the personal update link we email them. To exercise any of these, write to <email>hej@nordicmedialab.dk</email>. If you are ever unhappy with how we have handled your data, you have the right to complain to the Danish Data Protection Agency (<dpa>Datatilsynet</dpa>).
privacy.changes: If we change how we handle data, we will update this page and, for anything significant, tell members directly.
